findings.title: No physical address detected on homepage
findings.summary: polarmountainhvac.com homepage does not appear to display a business address.
findings.whyItMatters: NAP (Name, Address, Phone) consistency is a core local SEO signal. Google uses address presence to confirm local relevance and to match you with map listings.
findings.recommendation: Display your full business address in the site footer and on the homepage. Mark it up with LocalBusiness schema for extra credit.
findings.impactReason: NAP consistency across the web and homepage is a local ranking factor
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Weaker local pack signals; users can't confirm the business location

findings.title: No map embed or directions link found
findings.summary: No Google Maps embed or "Get Directions" link was detected anywhere on the site.
findings.whyItMatters: A map embed reinforces physical location signals, helps mobile users get directions instantly, and contributes to local relevance signals for Google.
findings.recommendation: Embed a Google Maps iframe on the contact page. Also add a "Get Directions" button linked to your Google Maps listing.
findings.impactReason: Embedded maps reduce friction for customers who want to visit in person
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Increased drop-off from intent-to-visit users; lost foot traffic

findings.title: No business hours found on the site
findings.summary: No business hours information was detected across all scanned pages.
findings.whyItMatters: Hours are a core conversion signal — users need to know if you're open before they call. Google also uses hours from your site to cross-validate Google Business Profile data.
findings.recommendation: Display your hours on the homepage, contact page, and in the footer. Add `openingHoursSpecification` to your LocalBusiness schema.
findings.impactReason: Users can't determine if the business is open before calling or visiting
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Lost leads who move to a competitor that shows hours clearly

findings.title: No location or service-area pages found
findings.summary: The site appears to have no pages targeting specific cities or service areas.
findings.whyItMatters: Without location-specific pages, the site cannot rank for "[service] in [city]" searches. These are the highest-value local SEO searches for most service businesses.
findings.recommendation: Create dedicated pages for each primary service area (e.g., "/plumber-austin-tx/"). Each page should mention the city prominently and include NAP for that location.
findings.impactReason: Location-specific pages are critical for ranking in nearby cities and suburbs
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Zero geo-specific organic visibility outside the primary city

findings.title: 1 page missing an H1 heading
findings.whyItMatters: The H1 is the primary on-page heading — it tells both Google and visitors what the page is about. Pages without an H1 miss a key ranking signal.
findings.recommendation: Add a single, descriptive H1 to each page. For a service page it should name the service and ideally the location: "Roof Replacement in Austin, TX".
findings.impactReason: H1 is a primary on-page signal for topic relevance
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Minor ranking signal loss; pages may underperform for target keywords

findings.title: No contact form found on the site
findings.summary: No lead capture form was detected on any page.
findings.whyItMatters: Not every visitor is ready to call. A contact form captures leads from visitors who prefer to inquire by email, who are outside business hours, or who want to provide details before calling.
findings.recommendation: Add a contact/inquiry form to the contact page and ideally the homepage. Keep it short: name, phone, service needed, preferred callback time.
findings.impactReason: No site-wide forms means there is no async lead capture path
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: All leads must call or email directly; visitors who prefer forms are lost

findings.title: Hero section does not clearly communicate what the business offers
findings.summary: H1 exists but is below the fold: "THE BEST VALUE IN AIR CONDITIONING SERVICE & REPAIR IN TUCSO"
findings.whyItMatters: Visitors decide whether to stay or leave within seconds. A clear H1 headline stating what you do, where you do it, and what to do next dramatically reduces bounce rates from local searches.
findings.recommendation: Write an H1 that answers three questions: What do you do? Where do you serve? What should the visitor do? Example: "Expert Roof Repairs in Dallas, TX — Call for a Free Estimate."
findings.impactReason: An unclear hero message means visitors don't immediately know what the business offers
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Higher bounce rate from confused first-time visitors

findings.title: 2 pages with multiple H1 headings
findings.summary: 2 page(s) have more than one H1 tag.
findings.whyItMatters: Multiple H1s dilute the page's topical focus signal. Google prefers one clear H1 per page.
findings.recommendation: Keep exactly one H1 per page. Downgrade additional H1s to H2 or H3.
findings.impactReason: Multiple H1s send mixed topical signals but rarely cause significant ranking drops
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Minor on-page optimization loss; easy to fix for small gains

findings.title: Only one service page found
findings.summary: The site has only one page classifiable as a service page.
findings.whyItMatters: Each unique service you offer deserves its own page. A single service page limits your Google footprint and forces all keywords to compete on one URL.
findings.recommendation: Create individual pages for each service you offer. Use a clear URL structure: /service-name/ or /service-name-city/.
findings.impactReason: Some service pages exist but don't cover all offered services
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Partial keyword coverage; some high-intent searches go unanswered

findings.title: 1 service page is thin on content
findings.whyItMatters: Thin service pages are hard to rank. Google looks for content depth to confirm the page genuinely covers the topic. Thin pages also fail to build confidence with potential customers.
findings.recommendation: Expand each service page to at least 200 words. Cover: what the service is, how it works, why choose you, what areas you serve, FAQs, and a strong CTA.
findings.impactReason: Service pages exist but lack depth to outperform competitors in rankings
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Weak keyword relevance on service pages; ranking potential is limited

findings.title: No location or service-area pages found
findings.summary: No pages targeting specific cities or service areas were detected.
findings.whyItMatters: "Plumber near me" and "[service] in [city]" are among the most valuable search queries for local businesses. Without location pages, you can't rank for these unless your domain authority is very high.
findings.recommendation: Create city/area pages for every location you serve. URL format: /[service]-[city]-[state]/. Each must have unique, helpful content — not just the same text with the city name swapped.
findings.impactReason: No location-specific content means no foothold in nearby city searches
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Missed organic traffic from high-intent "near me" and suburb-specific queries

findings.title: No gallery or portfolio page found
findings.summary: No gallery, portfolio, or before/after page was detected.
findings.whyItMatters: For trade businesses (roofers, remodelers, landscapers, etc.) and beauty services, showing your work is one of the strongest trust signals available. "Show, don't tell."
findings.recommendation: Add a gallery, portfolio, or "Our Work" page with photos of real completed jobs. For each image, add a descriptive alt text (e.g., "roof replacement Austin TX") for SEO benefit.
findings.impactReason: Gallery pages help visual businesses but are not a universal conversion factor
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Missed opportunity to showcase work quality; affects visually-driven decisions

findings.title: No visible trust signals near the top of the homepage
findings.summary: No trust signal keywords near top of page
findings.whyItMatters: Trust signals (star ratings, review counts, "Licensed & Insured") reduce hesitation for first-time visitors. Their absence makes the site feel less credible than competitors who display them prominently.
findings.recommendation: Add a trust bar below the hero section: number of Google reviews + star rating, years in business, license/insurance status, and any industry certifications.
findings.impactReason: Trust signals hidden below the fold are rarely seen before users decide to leave
findings.estimatedBusinessEffect: Trust content is not doing its job; conversion rate is lower than it should be

findings.title: No Google Maps embed found
findings.summary: No embedded Google Map was detected on any page of the site.
findings.whyItMatters: An embedded map reinforces the physical location to Google and helps visitors find the business — both improve local pack rankings.
findings.recommendation: Add a Google Maps embed to the contact page or homepage using the "Embed a map" option inside Google Maps.

findings.title: No Google review link on site
findings.summary: No link to the business's Google review page was found.
findings.whyItMatters: A direct review link reduces friction for happy customers. More Google reviews improve local pack rankings and build social proof.
findings.recommendation: Add a "Leave us a Google review" button to the site. Get the direct review URL from the Google Business Profile dashboard → "Get more reviews".

findings.title: Google Business Profile not found
findings.summary: This business does not appear to have a claimed Google Business Profile.
findings.whyItMatters: A Google Business Profile is the #1 local SEO factor. Without one, the business cannot appear in the Local Pack (the map results at the top of Google for local searches).
findings.recommendation: Claim or create a Google Business Profile at business.google.com. Verify the listing, add photos, and complete all profile fields.

roadmap.title: Add your address, hours, and a map to make your location easy to find
roadmap.whyItMatters: Local customers need to know where you are, when you are open, and how to get there. If this information is missing or buried, visitors will go to a competitor whose website answers these questions immediately.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Add your full address and business hours to your homepage and contact page. Embed a Google Map so visitors can get directions with one click. If you serve multiple areas, create a dedicated page for each location.

roadmap.title: Write more detailed pages that explain your services and service area
roadmap.whyItMatters: Thin pages with little content rarely rank well because Google struggles to understand what you offer and for whom. Competitors with detailed service pages consistently outrank sites with sparse content.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Create or expand your service pages to clearly describe each service, who it is for, and why customers should choose you. Add a dedicated page for each major service and each city or town you serve. Aim for at least 300–500 words per page.

roadmap.title: Make it immediately clear who you are and why visitors should stay
roadmap.whyItMatters: The first thing a visitor sees on your homepage determines whether they stay or leave. If there is no clear headline, photo, or trust signal above the fold (before scrolling), many visitors will bounce without ever learning about your services.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Update your homepage hero section to include: a clear headline stating what you do and where, a short sub-heading with your key selling point, a visible phone number or CTA button, and a recognizable photo (your team, your work, or your location).

roadmap.title: Fix missing or poorly written page titles and descriptions
roadmap.whyItMatters: Page titles and descriptions are what Google shows in search results. If they are missing, duplicated, or too short, your pages look generic and get passed over for competitors who have written compelling, keyword-rich summaries.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Give every page a unique title (50–60 characters) that describes exactly what the page is about, including your service and city. Write a short description (150–160 characters) for each page that encourages someone to click. Make sure every page has exactly one clear main heading.

roadmap.title: Add a contact form so people can reach you any time of day
roadmap.whyItMatters: Not everyone wants to call — many visitors prefer to send a message, especially outside business hours. Without a contact form you are missing enquiries from people who would have hired you.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Add a simple contact form to your contact page and ideally your homepage too. Ask only for the essentials: name, phone or email, and a brief message. Make sure form submissions arrive in an inbox you check regularly.

roadmap.title: Build visible credibility so visitors trust you before they call
roadmap.whyItMatters: Visitors decide within seconds whether a business looks trustworthy. Without reviews, credentials, photos, or an About page, many people will leave rather than risk contacting an unknown company.
roadmap.plainEnglishFix: Add real customer reviews or testimonials to your homepage. Create an About page that introduces your team and story. Add photos of your work, vehicle, or premises. If your site is not yet on HTTPS (the padlock), ask your hosting provider to enable SSL — it is usually free.

seoOpportunities.title: Split Generic Services Page into Individual Pages
seoOpportunities.description: You have one generic services page but competitors have multiple individual service pages. Each dedicated page can rank for its own set of local keywords.
seoOpportunities.reason: Google ranks specific pages higher for specific searches. A page titled "Kitchen Remodeling" will rank for "kitchen remodeling near me" far better than a generic services page.
